newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard says seeks peaceful waterfront.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard says seeks peaceful waterfront.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday the government had plans to reform the nation's waterfront industry but sought no confrontation with the union movement over the issue.
"We would never want to crush a union. We do want to crush low productivity anywhere in the Australian economy," Howard told reporters at Cleveland in suburban Brisbane.
"We do seek a more efficient waterfront. We don't seek confrontation," Howard said.

"But we are prepared in that (waterfront) area as in a lot of other areas of the Australian economy to see the enormous benefits of the workplace relations act reforms flow through without interruption and without hindrance," Howard said.
He said that had implications for the waterfront and the impact of productivity levels on the waterfront.

Howard denied there was a federal government "battle plan" for waterfront reform. "The government always has plans but I don't want you to see any of those plans in a belligerent context," he said. "That would misrepresent us grievously."
